findings.issue_text: [BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which this PR reroutes through the new MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() override to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — a method that throws UnsupportedOperationException — while the gate added in the same hunk only checks Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, which does not exclude the V2 evaluator that AdminPermissions.management() installs when the V2 feature is on. In any deployment where both admin-fine-grained-authz feature flags are enabled (e.g. an existing V1 permissions user trying V2), deleting any client throws UnsupportedOperationException out of the provider-event listener inside session.clients().removeClient(), so DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with a 500 and the client cannot be deleted; the new tests never exercise this because they only run the V2 feature profile where the V1-flag gate hides the throw.

[BUG] canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2") instead of returning a decision, but it is the runtime permission check the token-exchange flow invokes via AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...) on every exchange request. With the V2 feature and the token-exchange feature enabled, every token-exchange request fails with HTTP 500 — whereas V1 returns true when the target client has no permissions enabled — instead of being permitted or denied with a 403; the not-implemented marker must be fail-closed (return false) or an actual evaluation, never a throw on a live protocol endpoint.

[ADVISORY] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles are the only V2 overrides with no admin-role short-circuit — canManage(client), canManageClientScopes and canView(clientScope) all return true for holders of MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS via root.hasOneAdminRole — so a MANAGE_CLIENTS admin gets canManage(client)=true but canMapRoles(client)=false. Unless every role-mapping call site adds its own canManage fallback (V1's isPermissionsEnabled-based fallback is gone — V2 throws from isPermissionsEnabled), enabling V2 locks standard client admins out of all role mapping with 403s; no test in the diff runs any admin-role holder under V2, so this lockout would ship silently.

[ADVISORY] V2 ships no cleanup for the per-client "Clients" resources that AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates when a client-scoped permission is granted: setPermissionsEnabled throws instead of deleting the resource, and the only cleanup path (the ClientRemovedEvent listener) is now gated on the V1 feature flag. Under V2, every client deleted after being granted a permission leaves its resource and attached policies orphaned in the authorization store; getClientsWithPermission iterates and re-evaluates each orphan via hasGrantedPermission on every subsequent clients-list call, so V2 realms accumulate unbounded stale resources and pay for their policy evaluation on each list request.

[ADVISORY] The private method getEvaluationContext has no call sites in the new class (its only plausible consumer, canExchangeTo, throws before using it) and the logger field is never read — dead leftovers of the unimplemented token-exchange path. Maintainers reading ClientPermissionsV2 are misled into believing exchange-permission evaluation is implemented and must trace the UnsupportedOperationException throws to discover it is not; delete getEvaluationContext, the logger field, and their now-unused imports (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext, Logger).

[ADVISORY] The "does any granted permission carry this scope" loop is copy-pasted three times — hasPermission(ClientModel,String) at 224-234, hasPermission(String) at 249-259, and hasGrantedPermission at 276-283 — with two different idioms (Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s) in the first two versus scope.equals(s) in the third). The next change to permission-scope matching (the security-critical part of this class) must be replicated in three places that have already drifted idiomatically; extract a single hasScope(Collection<Permission>, String) helper and delete roughly 15 duplicated lines.

[BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 evaluate only hasPermission(client, ...) with no admin-role check, breaking the pattern every other override in this class follows (canManage(ClientModel) short-circuits on MANAGE_CLIENTS, canView() covers VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS via canViewClientDefault), so an admin holding the realm-management manage-clients role is denied all client role-mapping operations. In a realm where the V2 evaluator is active, an admin with the MANAGE_CLIENTS role — who can still manage, view and configure every client through this same class — gets 403 when adding client-level role mappings to a user or adding composites, because those endpoints consult canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles (the diff's own testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient proves the operations only succeed once MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE permissions exist) and hasPermission returns false when no explicit permission was created; V1 granted MANAGE_CLIENTS across all client scopes, so this silently revokes a core admin capability on upgrade, and no test in the diff exercises any role-holding admin against the V2 client evaluator to catch it.

[BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but this same diff defines ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled to throw UnsupportedOperationException and adds no other cleanup for the per-client 'Clients' authorization resources that AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveClient create, so client deletion has no working cleanup path under V2. Deleting a client in a realm with V2 admin permissions either throws UnsupportedOperationException out of the event listener and fails the DELETE with a 500 (when management() resolves MgmtPermissionsV2, the resolution the admin evaluator uses in exactly these realms), or silently orphans the resource named by the client's internal ID plus every scope permission attached to it (when the V1 MgmtPermissions is resolved, it only manages the legacy realm-management resource server) — and the orphaned IDs keep flowing out of getClientsWithPermission into the clients-list filter; testManageAllClients deletes only 'newClient', which has no per-client permission, so the diff verifies neither failure mode.

[ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope is wired into the schema constant, the CLIENTS resource-type scope set and canMapClientScopeRoles, but nothing in the diff verifies it: PermissionClientTest statically imports and dedicates tests to CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, yet no test creates a map-roles-client-scope permission or exercises any operation it gates. A regression in the MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE evaluation — or the discovery that no endpoint ever calls canMapClientScopeRoles, leaving the scope inert — ships undetected, and the first admin to configure a map-roles-client-scope permission finds it silently fails closed with no test defining what correct behavior even is.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 ships unreachable dead code: the private getEvaluationContext has no caller (its only conceivable caller canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException on its first line), and the logger field and the static TOKEN_EXCHANGE import are never referenced anywhere in the class. The next maintainer must reverse-engineer whether token-exchange evaluation is live in V2 (it is not) before safely touching this class, and the unused import/field are lint noise; deleting getEvaluationContext together with its ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports removes ~20 lines with zero behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The javadoc added for the void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() states 'Returns true if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true' — copy-pasted from the can* variants — while every other require* method in this same diff documents 'Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false'. Implementers and callers reading the evaluator contract get a nonsensical returns-clause for two of the permission-check methods and no statement of the actual throw behavior, undermining the contract documentation this diff exists to add.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission invokes hasGrantedPermission — a full root.evaluatePermission policy evaluation — for every resource of type Clients on each call, so the clients-list filtering path performs one complete authorization evaluation per per-client permission resource, per request. A realm that grants per-client permissions at scale turns every admin clients-list request by a non-view-all admin into N full policy evaluations (each loading and evaluating policies from the store), degrading the admin console client list linearly with the number of permission-enabled clients.

[ADVISORY] The @AfterEach cleanup removes only the scope permissions, not the per-client 'Clients' resources that permission creation materializes through AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, so the authorization resources created in one test method persist into every later method of the class. hasPermission takes the per-client-resource branch instead of the all-clients fallback for myclient in whichever tests run after the first one, so the code path under test depends on JUnit method ordering and the next test added to this class inherits invisible state from its siblings.

[BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles return only hasPermission(...), omitting the root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) short-circuit that canManage(client), canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) in the same class all perform. An admin holding only the manage-clients realm role is denied every client role-mapping operation (requireMapRoles -> canMapRoles -> hasPermission returns false when no fine-grained permission is configured, since server==null and empty policy lookups both yield false) while canManage(client) grants that same admin full manage and delete rights on the identical client - coarse-grained role mapping breaks under the V2 evaluator, and the diff's own test (testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient) confirms the mapping endpoints consult clients().canMapRoles.

[BUG] Gating the role/client/group removal-cleanup listener on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) while this same PR makes MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() return ClientPermissionsV2 (whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException) leaves no configuration in which permission resources are cleaned up: where the gate passes and V2 is the active evaluator, ClientRemovedEvent/RoleRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent dispatch into the throwing V2 methods; where the gate skips, the cleanup never runs at all. Deleting a client, role or group in a realm running the V2 evaluator either fails with an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException from the event listener (500 on the delete) or silently orphans the object's authz resource and every scope permission/policy referencing it - the store accumulates dead resources indefinitely and getClientsWithPermission hands ids of deleted clients to permission-filtered listing callers.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2 implements the entire per-client permission lifecycle surface (setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission/viewPermission/configurePermission/mapRoles*Permission) as unconditional UnsupportedOperationException throws, so the V2 evaluator ships no mechanism to remove a deleted client's permission resource. A client deleted after being granted a fine-grained permission leaves its resource (named by the client id, per resolveClient) and all scope permissions referencing it permanently orphaned in the authorization store; the orphans are iterated by getClientsWithPermission's findByType(CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) scan on every permission-filtered client listing, returning stale ids for clients that no longer exist.

[BUG] canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException unconditionally while remaining the concrete implementation returned by MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(), so the inherited token-exchange permission hook has no V2 implementation. Any token-exchange flow that consults the client permission evaluator while V2 is active receives an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (a 500) instead of a grant/deny decision, and the same applies to every retained V1 caller of the per-client permission-management methods (managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRolesPermission, resource, getPermissions) - nothing in the diff gates those callers away from the V2 instance.

[ADVISORY] The private getEvaluationContext builder is dead code - no method in the class calls it because canExchangeTo throws before any evaluation - and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import (line 46) and the logger field (line 51) are likewise unused. The next maintainer implementing token-exchange evaluation in V2 must reverse-engineer whether this orphaned builder is the intended hook (its presence implies exchange support that the throwing canExchangeTo disproves), and roughly 25 lines plus four imports can be deleted outright.

[ADVISORY] Three near-identical evaluate-and-match loops (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String), hasGrantedPermission) duplicate the permission-matching logic with observed drift: hasGrantedPermission matches with scope.equals(s) while the other two use expectedScopes.contains(s), and only the per-client overload carries the all-clients type-resource fallback. The next change to scope matching or to the all-clients fallback must be replicated across three private methods; missing one produces silently divergent permission decisions between the per-client, all-clients and listing paths - the copies have already drifted in both matching style and null-fallback behavior.

[ADVISORY] The new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope and its evaluator method canMapClientScopeRoles are exercised by no test in the diff - testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE but never MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE and never performs a client-scope role-mapping operation. A regression in client-scope role-mapping enforcement - or the scope being entirely absent from the enforcement path, leaving it a ships-inert schema entry - ships undetected; admins who grant map-roles-client-scope get silently non-functional permissions.

[ADVISORY] testManageOnlyOneClient permanently mutates the class-shared managed realm (renames myclient via update and moves a default client scope to optional via removeDefaultClientScope/addOptionalClientScope) and testConfigureOnlyOneClient rotates the client secret, while the @AfterEach cleanup removes only scope permissions - the shared state is never restored. The tests in PermissionClientTest are coupled through mutated shared state, so the next test added to the class (or any change in JUnit method order) that assumes myclient's pristine name, secret or default-scope layout fails depending on execution order.

[BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles are the only per-client overrides in ClientPermissionsV2 with no admin-role short-circuit, and their sole path hasPermission() returns false whenever isAdminSameRealm() is false or the realm has no authorization resource server, so under V2 no admin-role holder can map client roles without an explicit FGAP grant. With the V2 evaluator active, the default master-realm admin (isAdminSameRealm() == false makes hasPermission unconditionally false) and any same-realm admin holding MANAGE_CLIENTS in a realm without configured fine-grained permissions gets 403 on every role-mapping, composite and client-scope-role operation, while the same class lets those exact callers manage, view and configure the same clients — a regression from V1 where admin roles authorize role mapping.

[BUG] setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the ClientRemovedEvent handler this same diff touches (AdminPermissions.java:92) calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every client removal when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, so client deletion crashes under the V2 evaluator this diff wires into MgmtPermissionsV2.clients(). Deleting any client in a realm where the V2 evaluator is active together with the gating feature flag throws UnsupportedOperationException from inside the model-event dispatch and the delete fails with a 500; before this diff MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returned the inherited V1 implementation that performed this cleanup without throwing.

[BUG] The diff gates the entire role/client/group removal-cleanup listener on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ alone, so in any deployment where the V2 evaluator is active without that exact flag the cleanup never runs at all. Every client deleted under such a V2 deployment leaves the authorization resource this diff lazily creates via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource/resolveClient (named with the client's internal id) plus its attached scope permission permanently orphaned in the store, where it keeps appearing in the findByType iteration behind getClientsWithPermission and accumulates without bound.

[BUG] canExchangeTo — the permission gate for client-to-client token exchange — is implemented as throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"), so the live token-exchange path surfaces a raw exception instead of a grant/deny decision under V2. Any client-to-client token-exchange request reaching the permission check in a realm with the V2 evaluator active fails with an UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500 to the token-endpoint caller) instead of being permitted or cleanly denied, breaking token exchange for V2 realms.

[ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 substitutes throwing stubs for ten inherited V1-surface methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, viewPermission, configurePermission, mapRoles*Permission, exchangeToPermission) while remaining the concrete return type of MgmtPermissions.clients(), leaving every pre-existing caller outside this diff's evaluator surface on a crash path. Operators calling the still-advertised V1 management-permissions REST surface (e.g. /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/managementPermissions, which drives isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions/setPermissionsEnabled) against a V2 realm get HTTP 500s instead of a decision or a clean feature-not-supported response; nothing in the diff disables or versions those routes.

[ADVISORY] The per-client hasPermission falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource (resolving-or-creating the 'Clients' type resource) while the no-arg hasPermission at line 243 uses a read-only findByName and returns false when that resource is absent, so the two overloads disagree about whether an all-clients grant exists whenever the type resource has not been materialized. Any writer that creates a type-level Clients permission without first materializing the type resource (realm import, store-level provisioning) makes canManage()/canView()/canManageClientScopes() silently deny all-clients grants — list and create endpoints 403 — while per-client checks still honor the same grant; the get-or-create fallback also makes a permission evaluation write a store row on a read path.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission runs one full policy evaluation (root.evaluatePermission, reloading policies and scopes from the store) per resource of type Clients with no bound or short-circuit, and the type-level resource itself is included in the findByType iteration so its own name 'Clients' can be added to the returned set of client ids. Realms where fine-grained permissions are attached to many clients pay an O(N) policy-evaluation fan-out on every clients-list request that consults this method, degrading the admin console as FGAP adoption grows, and every consumer of the returned id set must tolerate the bogus 'Clients' entry.

[ADVISORY] The new class ships dead token-exchange scaffolding: getEvaluationContext is never called (canExchangeTo throws instead), and the static import of AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE (line 45) and the Logger field (line 50) are unused. The next maintainer must reverse-engineer whether the UnsupportedOperationException stub was meant to consume this evaluation context (i.e. token exchange is unfinished) or the method is orphaned; deleting the method, logger and import removes ~20 lines with no behavior change.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces a second hand-maintained copy of the client scope vocabulary — AdminPermissionsSchema.CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE — alongside the ClientPermissionManagement#CONFIGURE_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE_SCOPE constants that this diff's own javadoc still references for the same resource server. The two constant sets must stay string-equal for V2 evaluations to match V1-created scope entities, but nothing enforces it: a rename in one copy silently denies every permission of that scope at evaluation time (string comparison, no compile error), biting whoever edits either class next.

[ADVISORY] resolveClient resolves permission-target input by internal id first and user-chosen clientId second, so input carrying a client's clientId silently binds to a different client whose internal id equals that string. An admin granting a permission by clientId that happens to match another client's internal UUID (clientIds are unrestricted user-chosen strings) gets the resource named — and the permission applied — to the wrong client with no error; the diff replicates resolveUser's ambiguous two-key resolution into a new resource type where the secondary key is fully user-controlled.

[ADVISORY] The evaluate-then-match-scope loop is hand-copied three times (hasPermission(ClientModel,String) at 223-231, hasPermission(String) at 248-256, hasGrantedPermission at 275-282) and the copies have already drifted (Arrays.asList(scope).contains vs scope.equals). The next change to scope matching in the evaluator must be replicated in three places or the three permission paths silently disagree; extracting a single hasScope(Resource, String) helper deletes ~20 lines and the drift along with them.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff covers the two behaviors this diff puts at risk: testManageAllClients removes a client and asserts only that the list no longer contains it, never that the client's authorization resource was cleaned up, and no test exercises the map-roles/composite/client-scope checks with an admin-role holder. The PR's own suite stays green while the client-removal cleanup contract (throwing/gated-off setPermissionsEnabled) and the missing admin-role bypass in canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles ship unverified — exactly the paths that break for real admins and on real client deletion.

[BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles return only hasPermission(client, ...) with no AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS bypass, breaking the pattern every other override in this same class follows (canManage(client), canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) all check the admin role first). With the V2 evaluator active, an administrator holding the manage-clients role is denied client role mapping, composite addition and client-scope role assignment in any realm where no explicit Clients permission resource exists (the default), silently revoking the V1 capability where the admin role bypassed per-object permissions; the inherited getAccess(client) also reports map-roles:false for full admins, and the diff's own tests never exercise a role-holding admin on these paths so nothing catches it.

[BUG] canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the new Clients resource type defines no token-exchange scope, so the V2 schema cannot represent exchange permissions at all. The token-exchange exchange-to flow decides grants through ClientPermissionEvaluator.canExchangeTo; under V2 every such request dies with an UnsupportedOperationException surfaced as an HTTP 500 instead of an allow/deny decision, so enabling the feature silently kills token exchange for the realm — a working V1 capability removed by a PR whose stated objective is only adding a resource type.

[BUG] isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions all throw UnsupportedOperationException, but these are the evaluator methods behind the existing per-client management-permissions REST surface. GET/PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management-permissions (used by kcadm, scripts and any REST consumer) return a 500 under V2 instead of a 4xx 'not supported' response, breaking a published admin API endpoint the moment the feature is enabled.

[ADVISORY] getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is dead code — its only conceivable caller is canExchangeTo, which this same class makes throw — leaving copied V1 scaffolding (plus the never-used logger field and the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import) in the class. Maintainers reading the class conclude token-exchange evaluation is implemented and wired when it is not; the 13-line block (and its four imports) should be deleted or canExchangeTo implemented, and its presence masks the missing exchange support flagged above.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel,String) and hasPermission(String) each inline their own evaluate-then-match-scopes loop instead of calling the existing hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String) helper, and the copies have already drifted (Arrays.asList(scope).contains(...) versus the helper's scope.equals(s)). Any future change to scope matching (e.g., normalizing scope names versus IDs) must be replicated in three places in one class, and the divergent idioms show the copies are not being kept in sync; routing both through hasGrantedPermission deletes roughly 16 lines and one of the two matching idioms.

[ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every granted Clients-typed resource, which includes the type-level 'Clients' resource itself, so an all-clients grant puts the literal string 'Clients' into the returned client-ID set while yielding zero real client IDs. Any consumer enumerating permitted clients from this set receives a bogus non-ID entry and an empty effective set under an all-clients permission, so list-filtering or UI logic built on it shows no permitted clients despite the grant; the same listing tests pass only because they do not route through this method.

[ADVISORY] None of the five new tests exercise the V2 client-scope evaluator methods (canManageClientScopes, canManage(ClientScopeModel), canView(ClientScopeModel), canMapClientScopeRoles), getClientsWithPermission, or cleanup of per-client permission resources when a client that has one is deleted. A regression in any of these — the same missing-admin-role-bypass mistake already visible in the map-roles trio, or permission resources orphaned by client deletion that getClientsWithPermission keeps evaluating and returning — ships with no failing test, since the new tests only cover manage/configure/view/map-roles on a single client and all-clients grants.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, while the ClientRemovedEvent handler this same diff wires up (AdminPermissions.java:89-91, now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every client deletion and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns this throwing implementation, so V2 has no functional cleanup path for a deleted client's authorization resource. In any deployment where the V2 evaluator is the active MgmtPermissions implementation under the feature flag, deleting a client raises UnsupportedOperationException inside the model-event listener — DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with a 500 or the error is silently swallowed — and in every branch the deleted client's 'Clients'-type resource and its attached scope-permission policies are never removed, leaving orphaned authorization resources that getClientsWithPermission keeps enumerating as granted client IDs.

[BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException even though canExchangeTo is the permission decision Keycloak's token-exchange flow requests from the client permission evaluator, so a realm running the V2 evaluator has no token-exchange authorization path at all. With the V2 evaluator active, token-exchange requests and the admin operations that create or read the exchange permission fail with a 500 (UnsupportedOperationException) instead of an allow/deny decision — a live authentication flow is broken by a hard runtime exception rather than a guarded feature boundary, and the same throw pattern covers the rest of the inherited permission-management surface (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, viewPermission, mapRoles*Permission) for any legacy caller.

[BUG] getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every resource returned by findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), which also matches the type-level resource itself (named "Clients"), so the returned set of granted client IDs contains the phantom entry "Clients" for any caller holding a type-level Clients permission. Consumers that resolve the returned set as client identifiers — the permission-filtered client listing this override exists to serve — receive a bogus "Clients" entry that resolves to no client, producing phantom list entries or null-lookup failures; V1's equivalent set never contained such an entry because V1 had no type-level resource, so this diff changes the contract for every existing caller.

[BUG] The pre-grant negative check in testManageOnlyOneClient never executes removeDefaultClientScope: clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes() on line 148 throws ForbiddenException first (view is already proven denied by the toRepresentation() block on lines 134-139), so the catch on lines 151-152 asserts the listing call's failure and passes regardless of removeDefaultClientScope's own authorization. Deleting the manage/configure permission check from the default-client-scope removal endpoint — letting a permission-less admin strip default scopes from any client — is not caught: the ForbiddenException always originates from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes call, so this test green-lights an authorization bypass it claims to rule out.

[BUG] The rewritten feature-gated listener's ClientRemovedEvent branch (lines 90-92) calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which now resolves to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled — overridden in this same diff to throw UnsupportedOperationException — and no test in the diff asserts the listener's outcome (testManageAllClients deletes a client at PermissionClientTest.java line 274 yet asserts nothing about permission cleanup or the event's effect). In every realm with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, deleting a client dispatches an event whose handler throws UnsupportedOperationException — client removal aborts with an error, or where event dispatch swallows the exception the V1 permission-resource cleanup silently stops and stale authorization resources accumulate — and the suite passes in the swallowed case because nothing asserts post-removal permission state.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises canMapClientScopeRoles or grants the new map-roles-client-scope scope: PermissionClientTest.java (the diff's client-permission suite, fully visible in the diff) grants only MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java and AbstractPermissionTest.java contain no reference to MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE. A regression in the client-scope role-mapping check — or a scope-name mismatch between the schema constant and the evaluator string — ships undetected; admins relying on map-roles-client-scope to constrain role mappings through client scopes get silently wrong grants or denials with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient grants MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE and CONFIGURE in a single permission (line 359) and asserts only the positive path (lines 362-364), so no test in the diff verifies that addComposites is denied when the caller holds MAP_ROLES without MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE. A regression where composite-role addition checks only map-roles — letting an admin holding the lesser grant escalate privileges through composite roles — passes this test because the two scopes are never granted separately; the distinct enforcement of the new MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE scope, a core deliverable of this diff, is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The getClientByClientId fallback in resolveClient (lines 179-181) is never triggered by any test in the diff — every visible client permission references the internal UUID via myclient.getId() (PermissionClientTest.java), unlike the Users analog which the suite exercises with username references (PermissionRESTTest.resourcesTest), and AbstractPermissionTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java and UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java contain no client-permission-by-clientId case. An admin creating a client permission that references the client by its clientId string resolves through this unverified branch; a mis-resolution there (wrong lookup or wrong resource name) silently grants or denies the wrong client and no test fails.

[ADVISORY] The V2 overrides canManageClientScopes(), canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel) change client-scope authorization from role-only to permission-based, but no test in the diff invokes realm-level client-scope endpoints with the permission-only admin — the visible tests (PermissionClientTest.java, checked alongside PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java and AbstractPermissionTest.java) only touch per-client scope assignments, which route through canView(client)/canManage(client). A regression in permission-based client-scope CRUD authorization — type-level MANAGE/VIEW not reaching these overloads, or hasPermission evaluating the wrong resource — leaves client-scope create/delete/list wrongly open or wrongly closed for fine-grained admins, undetected by this diff's tests.

[BUG] Gating the only authorization-data cleanup path (the ClientRemovedEvent listener) on the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag orphans deleted clients' resources and policies in V2 deployments, which run with that flag disabled — and the V2 implementation the listener would otherwise call (ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled) throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of cleaning up. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 evaluate only hasPermission(client, ...) with no admin-role check, breaking the pattern every other override in this class follows (canManage(ClientModel) short-circuits on MANAGE_CLIENTS, canView() covers VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS via canViewClientDefault), so an admin holding the realm-management manage-clients role is denied all client role-mapping operations. In a realm where the V2 evaluator is active, an admin with the MANAGE_CLIENTS role — who can still manage, view and configure every client through this same class — gets 403 when adding client-level role mappings to a user or adding composites, because those endpoints consult canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles (the diff's own testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient proves the operations only succeed once MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE permissions exist) and hasPermission returns false when no explicit permission was created; V1 granted MANAGE_CLIENTS across all client scopes, so this silently revokes a core admin capability on upgrade, and no test in the diff exercises any role-holding admin against the V2 client evaluator to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, the overrides `canMapRoles(ClientModel)`, `canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel)`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` are implemented as only `hasPermission(client, <scope>)` with no admin-role short-circuit (unlike `canManage(ClientModel)` which explicitly returns true for `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` and `canView()` which covers admin roles via `canViewClientDefault()`). As a result, any code path that consults these `canMap*` methods will deny (403) callers who rely solely on the realm-management `MANAGE_CLIENTS` role unless explicit fine-grained permissions were created for MAP_ROLES* scopes. The added test `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` demonstrates these operations are gated by MAP_ROLES/MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE-style permissions and only succeed after such permissions are created, which aligns with this denial risk for role-based admins under V2.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `canExchangeTo(...)` and all related token-exchange permission methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException`, and there is no call site in this diff for `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] hasPermission(ClientModel,String) and hasPermission(String) each inline their own evaluate-then-match-scopes loop instead of calling the existing hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String) helper, and the copies have already drifted (Arrays.asList(scope).contains(...) versus the helper's scope.equals(s)). Any future change to scope matching (e.g., normalizing scope names versus IDs) must be replicated in three places in one class, and the divergent idioms show the copies are not being kept in sync; routing both through hasGrantedPermission deletes roughly 16 lines and one of the two matching idioms.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2, both hasPermission(ClientModel,String) and hasPermission(String) duplicate the same “evaluatePermission then iterate scopes” logic (building expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope) and checking expectedScopes.contains(s)) instead of reusing the existing hasGrantedPermission(Resource,String) helper, which already encapsulates the scope match (scope.equals(s)). This is diff-grounded duplication within the same class and creates an easy-to-miss maintenance hazard: any future change to scope matching would need updating in multiple places and the different matching idioms show drift potential, even if current behavior is effectively equivalent for a single scope string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every granted Clients-typed resource, which includes the type-level 'Clients' resource itself, so an all-clients grant puts the literal string 'Clients' into the returned client-ID set while yielding zero real client IDs. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new V2 client authorization logic (e.g., new scopes/resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema, new ClientPermissionsV2 with getClientsWithPermission and client-scope-related methods like canManageClientScopes/canView(ClientScopeModel)/canManage(ClientScopeModel)/canMapClientScopeRoles). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, while the ClientRemovedEvent handler this same diff wires up (AdminPermissions.java:89-91, now gated on Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every client deletion and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns this throwing implementation, so V2 has no functional cleanup path for a deleted client's authorization resource. In any deployment where the V2 evaluator is the active MgmtPermissions implementation under the feature flag, deleting a client raises UnsupportedOperationException inside the model-event listener — DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with a 500 or the error is silently swallowed — and in every branch the deleted client's 'Clients'-type resource and its attached scope-permission policies are never removed, leaving orphaned authorization resources that getClientsWithPermission keeps enumerating as granted client IDs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an internal inconsistency: AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In the same diff, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is overridden to return a ClientPermissionsV2 instance, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. Therefore, in any code path where management(...) yields MgmtPermissionsV2 under the feature flag, deleting a client will trigger an UnsupportedOperationException in the listener instead of performing cleanup, and the diff provides no alternative cleanup path in V2.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException even though canExchangeTo is the permission decision Keycloak's token-exchange flow requests from the client permission evaluator, so a realm running the V2 evaluator has no token-exchange authorization path at all. With the V2 evaluator active, token-exchange requests and the admin operations that create or read the exchange permission fail with a 500 (UnsupportedOperationException) instead of an allow/deny decision — a live authentication flow is broken by a hard runtime exception rather than a guarded feature boundary, and the same throw pattern covers the rest of the inherited permission-management surface (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, viewPermission, mapRoles*Permission) for any legacy caller.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `ClientPermissionsV2` overrides multiple `ClientPermissions` methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`, including `canExchangeTo(...)`, `exchangeToPermission(...)`, and several permission-management methods (`mapRoles*Permission`, `managePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). If any existing/legacy code path calls these while `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is active (as wired in `MgmtPermissionsV2`), it would indeed result in a 500 due to an unchecked exception rather than an allow/deny decision. However, the finding’s specific claim that Keycloak’s token-exchange flow necessarily calls `ClientPermissionEvaluator.canExchangeTo` in the V2 evaluator context (and that admin operations to create/read exchange permission will fail) is not verifiable from this diff alone, since no call sites are shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every resource returned by findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), which also matches the type-level resource itself (named "Clients"), so the returned set of granted client IDs contains the phantom entry "Clients" for any caller holding a type-level Clients permission. Consumers that resolve the returned set as client identifiers — the permission-filtered client listing this override exists to serve — receive a bogus "Clients" entry that resolves to no client, producing phantom list entries or null-lookup failures; V1's equivalent set never contained such an entry because V1 had no type-level resource, so this diff changes the contract for every existing caller.
matched_golden_ids: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both identify that getClientsWithPermission is returning resource.getName() from resources found by type (including the type-level "Clients" resource), but consumers expect real client IDs for lookup (e.g., realm.getClientById). This can introduce a bogus "Clients" entry / missing per-client IDs and lead to null lookups or incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The pre-grant negative check in testManageOnlyOneClient never executes removeDefaultClientScope: clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes() on line 148 throws ForbiddenException first (view is already proven denied by the toRepresentation() block on lines 134-139), so the catch on lines 151-152 asserts the listing call's failure and passes regardless of removeDefaultClientScope's own authorization. adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient()`, the pre-grant negative check meant to validate denial of `removeDefaultClientScope` is structured as `clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)` followed by `clientResource.removeDefaultClientScope(...)` inside the same `try`. This makes the catch/assert block succeed based on the listing call failing, and the test does not actually verify authorization on the removal endpoint, leaving a potential bypass untested.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest#testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, the client permission is created with scopes Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE) in a single permission, and the test only exercises the allowed paths (role mapping and addComposites) after granting both scopes together. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getClientByClientId fallback in resolveClient (lines 179-181) is never triggered by any test in the diff — every visible client permission references the internal UUID via myclient.getId() (PermissionClientTest.java), unlike the Users analog which the suite exercises with username references (PermissionRESTTest.resourcesTest), and AbstractPermissionTest.java, PermissionRESTTest.java and UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java contain no client-permission-by-clientId case. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new resolveClient(KeycloakSession,String) method in AdminPermissionsSchema that first calls session.clients().getClientById(realm, id) and then falls back to session.clients().getClientByClientId(realm, id). In the added/modified tests, client permissions are created using internal UUIDs (e.g., PermissionClientTest uses myclient.getId() and realmClient.getId() when calling createPermission(..., resourceId, clientsType,...)), and there is no test that creates a client permission referencing a client by its public clientId string. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The V2 overrides canManageClientScopes(), canManage(ClientScopeModel) and canView(ClientScopeModel) change client-scope authorization from role-only to permission-based, but no test in the diff invokes realm-level client-scope endpoints with the permission-only admin — the visible tests (PermissionClientTest.java, checked alongside PermissionRESTTest.java, UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java and AbstractPermissionTest.java) only touch per-client scope assignments, which route through canView(client)/canManage(client). A regression in permission-based client-scope CRUD authorization — type-level MANAGE/VIEW not reaching these overloads, or hasPermission evaluating the wrong resource — leaves client-scope create/delete/list wrongly open or wrongly closed for fine-grained admins, undetected by this diff's tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new permission-based logic specifically for client-scope authorization in V2 by overriding ClientPermissionEvaluator methods `canManageClientScopes()`, `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` in `ClientPermissionsV2` (new file), changing behavior from role-only to also allowing type-level permissions via `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE/VIEW)`. The newly added/modified tests in `PermissionClientTest` and the adjusted helpers in `AbstractPermissionTest` exercise per-client operations (e.g., `clients().get(id).getDefaultClientScopes()`, add/remove default/optional scopes, protocol mappers, role mapping) which primarily route through `canView(ClientModel)` / `canManage(ClientModel)` / `canConfigure(ClientModel)`, but do not invoke realm-level client-scope CRUD/list endpoints that would rely on the new `*ClientScopes` / `ClientScopeModel` overloads. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Gating the only authorization-data cleanup path (the ClientRemovedEvent listener) on the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ flag orphans deleted clients' resources and policies in V2 deployments, which run with that flag disabled — and the V2 implementation the listener would otherwise call (ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled) throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of cleaning up. In any realm using the V2 admin-permissions feature (the configuration this PR's own tests run under, where the legacy flag is off — evidenced by testManageAllClients deleting a client successfully despite the V2 setPermissionsEnabled throwing), deleting a client leaves its Clients-type resource, the scope-permission policies attached to it, and their referenced user policies permanently in the authorization store; getClientsWithPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-144) then returns the deleted client's ID as a still-granted client, and no migration, sweep, or cascade exists to purge the stale rows — realms that had the legacy flag enabled and later toggled it off lose the unconditional cleanup the review base provided.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps *all* ProviderEvent cleanup handling (RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent) inside `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))` in `AdminPermissions.registerListener(...)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). That means when the flag is disabled, the ClientRemovedEvent path no longer runs at all, so any cleanup previously performed via `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` will never execute. Separately, in V2 `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(...)` explicitly throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). Therefore, for V2: either the listener is disabled (no cleanup), or if enabled it would call into an unsupported operation and fail. Given `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(...)` enumerates stored resources by type and returns their names, any stale client resources would indeed be observable as still-granted. The gating + unsupported implementation combination is a concrete broken behavior exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException while remaining the cleanup target of the ClientRemovedEvent listener (AdminPermissions.java:91 calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)), which resolves to this class in any deployment where the V2 management is active. In a deployment with both the legacy admin-fine-grained-authz flag and the V2 feature enabled — forced globally on any instance serving both V1-permission realms and V2 realms, since the flags are process-wide — every client deletion throws an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException out of the event listener, so DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fails with a 500 and the removal rolls back; before this diff the same call dispatched to the V1 ClientPermissions and deletion worked, so this diff turns a working core admin operation into a hard failure.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), ClientRemovedEvent triggers management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). This diff introduces MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. Therefore, in any runtime where management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2, client removal events will throw from the listener, potentially breaking client deletion/cleanup flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every Clients-typed resource, including the type-level resource created by getResourceTypeResource whose name is the literal string "Clients", so the returned set — which consumers treat as client IDs — mixes a sentinel non-ID with UUIDs and contains no actual client IDs under an all-clients grant. Whenever an all-clients scope permission exists (the createAllPermission flow this diff's tests exercise), the set contains only the string "Clients": a consumer filtering a client list by this set renders an empty list for an admin holding an all-clients grant, and a consumer resolving each returned ID attempts a client lookup for the nonexistent ID "Clients".

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission, the code iterates all resources of type AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients") and adds resource.getName() to the returned set. The type-level (all-clients) resource is also named "Clients" (see hasPermission(String) looking it up via findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)), so when only an all-clients permission exists (no per-client resources created), findByType will include that type-level resource and the returned set will include the literal "Clients" rather than actual client UUIDs. This mixes a non-client-id sentinel string with real IDs and cannot represent "all clients" as a set of client IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ClientPermissionsV2 ships dead code: the private getEvaluationContext method is unreachable because its only caller, canExchangeTo, throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the logger field (line 51) is never used. Maintainers reading the class are misled into believing token-exchange evaluation is wired up in V2 when it actually throws; the method, the logger, and the five imports they pull in (ClientModelIdentity, DefaultEvaluationContext, EvaluationContext, AccessToken, Logger) — roughly 20 lines — can be deleted with zero behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class, `private EvaluationContext getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` is never referenced anywhere in the diff, and the `private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(ClientPermissionsV2.class);` field is also unused. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The ClientRemovedEvent cleanup branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which this PR reroutes to ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195) — a stub that unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException — so in any deployment where the V2 evaluator is active, deleting a client raises that exception inside the removal flow when the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ gate (line 77) passes, and the cleanup is skipped entirely when the V2 feature runs without that flag. adjudication.rationale: In the listener added/modified in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch calls `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`. This PR introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is a stub that unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isPermissionsEnabled — together with the sibling overrides getPermissions, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, and managePermission at lines 172-205 — unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, but V1-era request paths still invoke these methods through AdminPermissions.management(): the /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/managementPermissions GET/PUT endpoints behind the admin console's client Permissions tab, and the token-exchange client-permission check, so in a V2-enabled deployment those requests return a raw 500 instead of the ManagementPermissionReference or boolean the contract promises. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The permission-scope matching loop is hand-copied three times (lines 224-233, 249-258, and 276-283) with drift already present — two copies use Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s) while hasGrantedPermission uses scope.equals(s). The next change to how granted scopes are matched (multi-scope requests, type-aware matching) must be replicated in three places; missing one makes the per-client check, the realm-level check, and the client-list filter return divergent decisions for the same permission.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2` there are three separate scope-matching loops: in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` the code builds `List<String> expectedScopes = Arrays.asList(scope)` and checks `expectedScopes.contains(s)`, while `hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String)` checks `scope.equals(s)`. Today these are equivalent for the current single-scope input, so it’s not a verifiable functional bug from the diff alone, but it is real duplication across three decision points (per-client, all-clients, and client-list filtering) that could easily diverge if matching semantics change later.
